bētācĕus , a, um, adj. 1. beta,
I.from or of the beet: “pedes betacei,” beet-roots, Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 27 .—Subst.: bētācĕus , i, m. (sc. pes), beet-root (cf. Charis. pp. 24 and 128 P.; Prisc. p. 618 ib.), Apic. 3, 2; Plin. Ep. 1, 15, 2 (where others, less correctly, read Baeticae); Arn. 4, p. 133 (others, betis).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
